srn_006: You can recognise it as the third of the cemetery's three cypresses, 2.70 metres round, standing behind the chapel at the gate on the main avenue. It stands in the Cimitero Comunale, Piano di Sorrento.
lux_005: You can recognise it as the surviving sequoia of a pair, the smaller at 27 metres and 4.58 metres round, after its larger twin came down to honey fungus in February 2026. It stands in Parc Amelie, beside the monument to Amalia.
ein_011: You can recognise it as the first tree inside the gate, standing beside the old caretaker's house. It stands in the Antonius kerkhof, Doelenstraat 2, Eindhoven.
gro_001: You can recognise it as the province's oldest tree, standing in front of the farmhouse at De Rollen. It is visible from Noorddijkerweg; the farm itself is private.
myz_002: You can recognise it by the opening in its trunk, leading to a hollow the size of a small room once used as a wartime air-raid shelter. It stands at the foot of the hill beside Funabiki Shrine, Kiyotake.
myz_003: You can recognise the largest by its angle, leaning behind the main hall, 9.6 metres round, on the side where the gate is usually shut. It stands in the precinct of Hachiman Shrine, Uryuno.
oss_003: You can recognise it as one of the few trees here with a precise planting year on record, 1928, rather than a decade band. It stands on Kloosterstraat, Megen.
oss_009: You can recognise it by its full, mature canopy, on the square where Klaphekkenstraat meets Goudmijnstraat. It stands in Oss.
